    Peptides for hair loss, compared with the proven options.

    Peptide Chooser editorial team. Last updated 30 Oct 2026. Every claim links to its source. Prices checked 30 Oct 2026.

    Finasteride and minoxidil are the only treatments on this page the FDA has approved for hair loss, and generic finasteride starts at about $10 a month. Copper peptide serums are cosmetics: the evidence is from lab and follicle-culture studies, not from large trials in people. Injectable peptides sold for hair are not approved for any use, and we found no human evidence for hair.

    For thinning hair, a receding hairline or bald spots: what slows the loss, what regrows hair, and what is only marketing.

    • Finasteride 1 mgFDA approvedProven alternative

      A daily pill. Slows hair loss and regrows some hair in most men; not for women who may become pregnant.

      FDA approved for hair loss.

      Prescription, from an online clinic or your doctor. From $10/mo (generic, pharmacy coupon).8

      Online clinicNo paid link yet
    • MinoxidilFDA approvedProven alternative

      A liquid or foam you put on the scalp twice a day. Regrows hair for men and women; works while you keep using it.

      FDA approved for hair loss.

      No prescription, any pharmacy. From $10/mo.9

      Online clinicNo paid link yet
    • GHK-Cu copper peptide serumCosmetic, no approval needed

      A cosmetic serum for the scalp. Small lab and follicle studies; no large trials in people.

      Cosmetic: legal to sell, nobody checked that it works.

      Sold in shops, no prescription.

      Vials from research-use shops, meant to be injected. No human evidence for hair.

    Is it legal today?

    FDA status of the peptides on this page, each with its source. Checked 30 Oct 2026.

    PeptideStatusWhat that means
    BPC-157Not approvedFDA advisory committee reviewed it for compounding on 23 Jul 2026; FDA proposed not to allow it 6
    GHK-Cu, Matrixyl, Argireline (creams and serums)Cosmeticcosmetics are regulated but do not need FDA approval to be sold 5
    TB-500Not approvedsame July 2026 review; FDA proposed not to allow it 6

    Approved means the FDA approved a product containing it for a stated use. Not approved means no approved product exists; buying it for yourself is not a crime in the US, but nobody has checked what is in the vial.
